speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to help determine the cause, have you noticed if these lesions are painful, itchy, or have they appeared elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced cutaneous mucosal blistering reaction (likely captopril-induced).

You recently started captopril and stopped meloxicam; given the onset of blisters on the forearm and painful mucosal ulcers (cheek and genital) one week later, this strongly suggests a new drug-induced hypersensitivity. Can you confirm if you have taken any other new medications or supplements in the last month, and do you have any history of similar reactions to ACE inhibitors or NSAIDs?
